predictive_observations: The time-sliced GeckoTerminal flow at decision time was buy-dominant. Subtracting m15 from h1 leaves about 11 buys against 69 sells in the earlier 45 minutes, then 133 buys against 92 sells in the last 15 minutes. m5 was also buy-heavy: 91 vs 78 on DexScreener and 67 vs 47 on GeckoTerminal, with 54 unique buyers against 39 unique sellers. Unlike the hourly totals, the most recent flow leaned toward buying.

Activity came out of near-dormancy. h6 volume was $41k, h1 was $37k and m15 was about $17.7k, so the five hours before had only about $4k. Unique buyers were 83 in m15 against 87 in h1. The burst was sudden and concentrated, and that fits fresh outside flow better than routine chop.

Deep liquidity ($1.5M, locked or burned) and no creator or dev holdings meant little risk of a structural collapse. That fits the observed MAE of -1.1% and the liquidity holding steady over 24h. The report's 'adequate' feasibility call was right.

The pre-trigger hourly sigma was about 3%. That should have told the analyst that a 'fade' call carries almost no information: a flat outcome was the base case, and the only question was whether a tail move would happen. The report's counterargument about legacy memes bouncing on rotation named the mechanism that apparently played out.
misleading_observations: 'In the last hour sells outnumbered buys (153 vs 107)' is an aggregate that hides a reversal inside the hour. The sell imbalance came before the trigger burst, and the burst itself was net buying.

Absence of a findable catalyst or news. The analyst couldn't see X (HTTP 402), and CEX-led or sector-rotation moves often have no token-specific catalyst. The report treated no evidence as evidence of absence.
Copy-paste airdrop promotion from Sept 15. It was a week old and says little about flows on Sept 22. It was used to label the whole move as promotional.
'99% off ATH, overhead supply'. That is a long-horizon structural fact with no measurable bearing on a 6h window.

Treating the DEX bump as small next to about $1M of mostly-CEX volume. That is a reason the DEX trigger was uninformative, not a reason to expect a fade. If price discovery happens on CEXs, the DEX burst may have been arbitrage carrying a CEX-led move up.
Static GMGN wallet-tag counts (69 smart, 125 renowned, 1000 whale or bundler) and the insider-cluster figures describe a 2-year-old token's history, not the current flow.
evidence_that_should_have_changed_conclu: Decomposing h1 into m15 and the remainder, which was possible from the packet, shows recent buy dominance and a dormancy break. That should have moved the view from 'fade' to at least 'uncertain'.

The packet contained no check of whether peer legacy Solana memecoins or the broader meme sector were moving at the same moment. Such a check was possible at decision time and bears directly on the rotation counterargument the report itself raised.
The analyst could not see X or CEX order flow, and CEX volume dominates. Those gaps argued for low confidence, not medium, on a directional fade.

The trade still moved +32% gross at 6h without any +50% touch. That move size needs flow the analyst couldn't observe, so better evidence would probably have changed confidence rather than flipping the call to a confident 'continue'.

hypotheses_proposed.statement: For triggered legacy tokens, the 6h forward return is positive more often than the universe baseline when m15 unique buyers are at least 80% of h1 unique buyers and m15 buys exceed sells. The same should not hold when the h1 aggregate is buy-dominant but m15 is not.
hypotheses_proposed.conditions: Pair age over 180 days, DEX liquidity over $500k, and a 'dormancy break': h6 volume minus h1 volume under 25% of h1 volume. Use only the GeckoTerminal/DexScreener windows available at decision time.
hypotheses_proposed.market_structure_rationale: When a deep, dormant pool suddenly concentrates activity with net buying, fresh outside flow has arrived. That flow may be CEX-led and carried over by arbitrage, or it may be rotation. Such flow tends to persist over hours, while hourly aggregates mix it with pre-burst noise.

hypotheses_proposed.statement: For tokens where DEX 24h volume is under 30% of all-venue 24h volume, the researcher's continue/fade call has no significantly better-than-chance agreement with the sign of the 6h return. Research confidence on these should be capped at low.
hypotheses_proposed.conditions: CEX-listed tokens whose all-venue volume can be retrieved at decision time, for example from CoinGecko.
hypotheses_proposed.market_structure_rationale: Price discovery happens on CEX order books the researcher can't see. The DEX trigger reflects arbitrage echoes, so DEX-only flow and social reads carry little directional information.

hypotheses_proposed.statement: For legacy memecoins, the median h1 return of a pre-defined peer basket of legacy Solana memecoins at decision time predicts the token's 6h return sign better than whether a token-specific catalyst was found.
hypotheses_proposed.conditions: Tokens over 180 days old with no identifiable token-specific news. The peer basket is fixed in advance and excludes the token itself.
hypotheses_proposed.market_structure_rationale: Moves in legacy memes are mostly driven by sector rotation and beta, not idiosyncratic narrative. So a catalyst search that returns nothing is weak evidence, while co-movement across peers is direct evidence of rotation flow.

structured_output.summary: The report called 'fade' at medium confidence. FWOG then rose about 30% net over 6h (MFE +44%, MAE -1.1%, and a 2-sigma up barrier hit in about 166 minutes), so the directional call was wrong. The sourcing was diligent, the canonical-token and feasibility assessments were right, and the counterargument named the likely mechanism (legacy-meme rotation). The main analytical error: the report leaned on the h1 sell imbalance while the packet's m15 and m5 windows showed the burst itself was buy-dominant and broke about five hours of dormancy. It also treated a missing catalyst as evidence, when X and CEX flow were invisible and most volume is on CEXs. Those gaps called for low confidence, not a confident fade. The size of the move probably depended on off-DEX flow the analyst could not see. So the outcome was only partly knowable: better reasoning should have produced 'uncertain' or low confidence, not necessarily a 'continue' call. One outcome is weak evidence either way, so the hypotheses above are meant to be tested on future cases.
